name: Tennant
metaTitle: Tennant Company (NYSE: TNC): Owner, Scrubbers and Cleaning Robots
legalEntityNote: Tennant Company is the listed operating company behind the Tennant equipment brand. The company, its IPC group brand, regional subsidiaries, distributors and model-specific technology partners should not be treated as interchangeable contracting, manufacturing or warranty entities.
headline: Tennant company, professional floor-cleaning portfolio, manufacturing and channels
description: A source-backed profile of Tennant Company, its professional floor-cleaning and autonomous equipment portfolio, global manufacturing footprint, sales channels and buyer verification points.
metaDescription: Tennant profile: listed-company identity, leadership, scrubbers, sweepers, autonomous equipment, manufacturing, channels, service and buyer checks.
quickAnswer: Tennant Company is an independent company listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TNC). It has no parent company.

faq.question: Who owns Tennant Company?
faq.answer: Tennant is an independent company listed on the New York Stock Exchange under TNC. Its filings identify no parent company.

faq.question: Where is Tennant headquartered?
faq.answer: Eden Prairie, Minnesota, in the United States. The company was founded in 1870.

faq.question: What does Tennant make?
faq.answer: Commercial and industrial floor scrubbers and sweepers, autonomous cleaning machines, and vacuums and extractors, with parts and service programmes. It also owns the IPC brand.

faq.question: Where does Tennant make its machines?
faq.answer: Tennant's 2025 annual report lists 11 global manufacturing locations. Check the serial plate and shipping documents for a specific machine's country of origin.

faq.question: How large is Tennant's robotics business?
faq.answer: Tennant reported robotics sales of approximately USD 37.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 71% from a year earlier, within total net sales of USD 322.3 million.

disclaimer: World Clean Biz is an independent industry publication and is not affiliated with Tennant Company. Company-level disclosures do not establish the manufacturer, origin, software provider, seller or warranty entity for every model and market.

ownership.summary: Tennant Company is a Minnesota corporation whose common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under TNC. The reviewed filings identify no parent company. Tennant also reports the IPC group brand within its business, but brand, subsidiary and regional seller responsibilities remain distinct.

leadership.name: Richard H. (Rusty) Zay
leadership.context: Appointed effective July 1, 2026, after serving as Chief Commercial Officer. The June 17 announcement assigns him oversight of customer-facing business units, supply chain, manufacturing, R&D and marketing.

productPortfolio.name: Floor scrubbers and sweepers
productPortfolio.positioning: Walk-behind, ride-on and compact machines cover commercial and industrial floor-maintenance applications.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Buyers should compare productivity, surface compatibility, batteries, consumables, operator training and local service support.

productPortfolio.name: Autonomous cleaning machines
productPortfolio.positioning: The ROVR and autonomous mobile robot portfolio adds repeatable robotic floor-cleaning workflows to staffed operations.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: Site mapping, safety validation, connectivity, software terms, uptime support and manual fallback must be evaluated alongside hardware.

productPortfolio.name: Vacuums, extractors, parts and service
productPortfolio.positioning: Commercial vacuuming, carpet care, genuine parts and service programs broaden Tennant beyond hard-floor machines.
productPortfolio.buyerRelevance: A fleet contract should specify parts availability, response times, preventive maintenance and the responsible regional service entity.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: Tennant's 2025 Form 10-K reports 11 global manufacturing locations supporting its commercial and industrial cleaning business.
manufacturingSupplyChain.scope: Tennant Company global network for the year ended December 31, 2025
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Verify the exact model's factory, country of origin, serial range and shipment documents; the global site count does not identify a specific SKU source.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: Tennant reports one operating and reportable segment covering the design, manufacture and marketing of cleaning solutions and related products.
manufacturingSupplyChain.scope: Company-level financial reporting, not a model-level manufacturing statement
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Request a bill of materials responsibility map and product compliance documents for the purchased model and market.

manufacturingSupplyChain.evidence: The X6 ROVR is marketed by Tennant as an autonomous floor scrubber within its ROVR product line.
manufacturingSupplyChain.buyerCheck: Confirm hardware manufacturer, autonomy software provider, data controller, cybersecurity support and replacement-parts responsibility in the contract.

marketsChannels.evidence: Tennant reports serving more than 40,000 customers through direct and distributor channels across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific.
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Verify whether the quotation comes from Tennant, a subsidiary or an authorized distributor and identify the contracting entity.

marketsChannels.evidence: Tennant publishes regional contact and location resources for sales, service and support.
marketsChannels.scope: Markets covered by Tennant's official regional websites and location directory
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Confirm technician coverage, response time, parts stock, commissioning capability and escalation contacts at the buyer's site.

marketsChannels.evidence: Tennant sells machines, parts and service while also working through distributors in selected markets.
marketsChannels.scope: Route-to-market model; exact coverage varies by country and product line
marketsChannels.buyerCheck: Obtain current distributor authorization and written warranty responsibility for the exact model and territory.

competitivePosition.summary: World Clean Biz assessment: Tennant is a focused global professional-cleaning specialist with a broad hard-floor portfolio, established service capabilities and a growing autonomous offer. Its differentiation is strongest where buyers value fleet uptime, application support and lifecycle service, while procurement still needs model- and market-specific checks for origin, software and channel responsibility.

developments.title: P1 VAC extends Tennant robotics into autonomous vacuuming
developments.summary: Tennant introduced P1 VAC, the first model in its P-Series, and said orders were open. The machine adds autonomous vacuuming and dust mopping to its robotic portfolio; the company describes this as its first autonomous soft-floor cleaner.

developments.title: Richard H. Zay becomes Chief Operating Officer
developments.summary: Tennant announced the appointment on June 17, with a July 1 effective date. Zay previously served as Chief Commercial Officer and has been on the leadership team since 2010.

developments.title: Tennant reports 2025 full-year results
developments.summary: The results update confirmed Dave Huml as CEO and provided current company performance and strategy context.

developments.title: Tennant reports an 11-site manufacturing network
developments.summary: The 2025 Form 10-K describes the company's global manufacturing and commercial footprint.
